study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dynamic gray matter volume changes in pediatric multiple sclerosis: A 3.5 year MRI study

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: NIHPD (NIH-funded MRI Study of Normal Brain Development) provided the longitudinal healthy control sample; SINGLE-SITE refers to the local healthy controls and pediatric MS patients recruited at Hospital San Raffaele (HSR).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: To overcome the difficulty of obtaining longitudinal MRI scans from pediatric HC, 2 groups of pediatric HC were selected for comparison of MRI volumes: (1) a group of 26 sex- and age-matched HC recruited at Hospital San Raffaele (HSR)... and (2) a group of 317 pediatric HC from the NIH-funded MRI Study of Normal Brain Development (NIH HC)

answer.SINGLE-SITE: normative training (HSR HC) and clinical research (pediatric MS patients)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: NIHPD data were used to estimate GM developmental trajectories. HSR HC were included in the same model to account for field strength differences. MS patients were compared against these trajectories to assess clinical deviations.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: To estimate normative sex- and age-expected GM growth curves... the following linear mixed-effects model was fitted voxel-wise to HC preprocessed GM maps... Another binary variable to account for differences in magnetic field strength ( MFSi ) and acquisition protocol was also added... to provide a standardized measure of the deviation from the normative expected value of each participant ' s GM volume... a z score map was computed

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The normative model used all healthy controls (26 from HSR and 317 from NIHPD) to estimate growth curves.
